title: Arithmologia, siue De abditis numerorum mysteriis
author: Athanasius Kircher
notes: Kircher's treatise on the hidden mysteries of numbers — Pythagorean, Hebraic/Cabalistic, and Christian theological numerology. 1665 first edition.

title: Oedipus Aegyptiacus, Vol. 1 (Tomus I)
author: Athanasius Kircher
notes: Volume 1 of Kircher's three-volume magnum opus on Egyptian hieroglyphs, hermetic philosophy, and the prisca theologia — the universal hieroglyphic doctrine he believed Moses, Hermes, and Pythagoras all shared. 1652 Rome edition.

title: Oedipus Aegyptiacus, Vol. 2 (Tomus II)
author: Athanasius Kircher
notes: Volume 2 of Oedipus Aegyptiacus — the heart of Kircher's hermetic synthesis. Contains his readings of Egyptian hieroglyphs and discussion of Hermetic, Pythagorean, Kabbalistic, and Persian traditions.

title: Oedipus Aegyptiacus, Vol. 3 (Tomus III)
author: Athanasius Kircher
notes: Volume 3 of Oedipus Aegyptiacus — Kircher's interpretations of specific obelisk inscriptions plus extended discussion of Egyptian theology, mythology, and ritual.

title: Musurgia Universalis, sive Ars Magna Consoni et Dissoni (Vol. 1)
author: Athanasius Kircher
notes: Volume 1 of Kircher's comprehensive treatise on music, acoustics, and harmonic mathematics. Includes his famous illustrations of musical instruments, mechanical music devices, and the music of the spheres.

title: Itinerarium Exstaticum (1656 first edition)
author: Athanasius Kircher
notes: First edition of Kircher's 'Ecstatic Journey' — Theodidactus, guided by an angel, travels through the spheres of the heavens. Written as a dialogue, it presents Tychonic cosmology and Kircher's vision of celestial worlds.

title: Lingua Aegyptiaca restituta
author: Athanasius Kircher
notes: Kircher's foundational work on Coptic and his claim to have decoded the ancient Egyptian language — a precursor to Oedipus Aegyptiacus. 1643 Rome edition.

title: Scrutinium Physico-Medicum contagiosae luis quae pestis dicitur
author: Athanasius Kircher
notes: Kircher's plague treatise (1658), notable for its early discussion of microscopic 'animalcules' as disease agents — among the first systematic suggestions of a microbial theory of contagion.

title: Latium, id est, Nova & parallela Latii tum veteris tum novi descriptio
author: Athanasius Kircher
notes: Kircher's antiquarian/topographical study of the region of Latium — ancient and modern. Lavishly illustrated. Getty Research Institute scan.

title: Sphinx Mystagoga
author: Athanasius Kircher
notes: Late Kircher treatise on hieroglyphic interpretation — a diatribe on the mystagogic sphinx. Continues the hermetic reading-strategy of Oedipus Aegyptiacus.

title: Ars Magnesia
author: Athanasius Kircher
notes: Kircher's first published work — on the nature, powers, and prodigious effects of the magnet. The foundation for his later, much-expanded Magnes (1641). PBC Gdańsk scan.
